My friend Daniel showed me round the club house.

words.w: show sb what to do/how to do sth

ex: The company plans to shut down four factories and cut 10 000 jobs.

ex: He was too shy to ask her to dance with him.

ex: There are at least two sides to every question.

ex: Whose side is he on?

I hope you'll be on my side.

senses.def: part of a situation that can be considered or dealt with separately
ex: She looks after the financial side of things.

ex: He read the letter and gave a deep sigh.
I entered the house with a deep sigh!

ex: She sighed deeply and sat down.

Having solid ground beneath her feet again she sighed with relief for having survived this adventure.

ex: If your sight is poor, you should not drive a car.
The old woman has lost her sight.

ex: You should always keep sight of your bags while you're at the airport.

The police officer was hidden out of sight behind a tree.
The castle came into sight as we went round a bend in the road.
We're looking for a house which is within sight of the mountains.

ex: She pointed to her watch as a sign that it was getting late and she wanted to leave.

ex: Flowers are the first sign of Spring.

ex: + and - are mathematical signs.

ex: I can't get a phone signal here.
